ast_eval.py.summary: Check Python files for syntax errors and quarantine the invalid ones.
details: Parses every file with ast, copies (or moves with ``-m``) the broken ones into an ``error`` folder beside them under a unique name and processes the tree in a starmap pool; ``--dry-run`` only reports.

atrans.py.summary: Translate a word list into a JSON mapping.
details: Reads one word per line, translates each of them with ``translate``, ``deep_translator`` or ``googletrans`` (falling back automatically), retries the failures, throttles the requests, saves the output periodically and collects the words that kept failing in ``failed.txt``.

autofix_typo.py.summary: Fix typos in text files with learned substitution patterns.
details: Learns the keyboard-adjacency and common-substitution patterns from a JSON database, proposes the corrections for the files of a directory and can apply them, optionally asking for confirmation and learning from each decision; ``--show-patterns`` dumps what was learned.

base64_extractor.py.summary: Extract the base64 data URIs of CSS, JS and HTML files into asset files.
details: Subcommands: ``extract-cleanuri`` rewrites the ``data:`` URIs as relative paths, ``extract-images``/``extract-css``/``extract-assets``/``extract-elements``/``extract-html`` pull the embedded assets out with magic-byte MIME detection, and ``file-to-base64``/``ttf-to-base64`` do the opposite. ``--hash``, ``--report``, ``--dry-run`` and ``--download-remote`` control the output.

bestwhois.py.summary: Query the WhoisXML API for a domain and print the record.
details: Reads the API key from the rc file or ``--apikey``, queries the service for the domain (Unicode or IDN), purges the empty fields and prints the record as coloured JSON or as plain text.

bhtml.py.summary: Beautify HTML files in parallel with js-beautify.
details: Runs ``html-beautify`` on the ``.html``/``.htm``/``.xhtml`` files (plus the suffixes passed with ``--ext``) through a temporary file and eight workers, logging only the warnings with ``--quiet``.

binarytools.py.summary: Move, sanity-check, verify and strip the binaries of a directory.
details: Subcommands: ``sort`` collects the binaries into a subfolder, ``sanity`` runs the executables and moves the broken ones (missing libraries) to an error folder, ``verify-so`` loads the shared objects with ctypes, and ``strip``/``size``/``ext``/``exclude``/``retry`` strip them by different selection rules.

bnn.py.summary: Replace the literal ``\n`` sequences of text files with real newlines.
details: Streams each text file in chunks (1 MB by default, ``-c`` changes it), replaces the escapes with line breaks through joblib in parallel and writes the result back with a per-file byte count.

brmc.py.summary: Strip the docstrings from Python files while keeping the module docstrings.
details: Removes the class and function docstrings with ast-driven source rewriting, validates that the result still parses and processes the tree in a pool.

c_build_tool.py.summary: Build the C, C++ and Cython sources of a directory in parallel.
details: Compiles each ``.c``/``.cpp``/``.cc``/``.cxx`` file with clang/clang++ (``--cflags`` passes extra flags, ``--strip`` strips the binaries), the ``cythonize`` subcommand builds the ``.pyx`` modules and the jobs run in a thread pool with a 60-second timeout.

camel2snake.py.summary: Refactor the camelCase identifiers of a Python tree to snake_case.
details: Collects the symbols with LibCST, rewrites the functions, classes, variables and parameters (``--targets``), can also rename the ``.py`` files, caches the work, snapshots an undo file and offers ``--undo``, ``--dry-run``, ``--diff`` and ``--exclude``.

cccpp.py.summary: Remove the comments from C and C++ sources with tree-sitter.
details: Deletes the comment nodes of the ``.c``/``.h``/``.cc``/``.cpp``/``.hpp`` files in place, either in batch with a process pool or with ``--interactive`` asking about each comment.

cext.py.summary: Extract the functions, classes and constants of Python files and archives.
details: Parses the sources with ast or tree-sitter, collects the module-level uppercase constants, writes each entity into a per-type output folder with the imports it needs and a ``global_imports`` module, and also reads the ``.py`` members of zip, wheel, tar and zstd archives in a worker pool.

check_conflicts.py.summary: Report the local files whose names collide with stdlib modules or PyPI packages.
details: Compares the ``.py`` file stems of a directory with the standard-library module names and the packages listed in ``/sdcard/data/pip.json`` (``--installed-only`` limits it to the installed distributions), writes ``conflict_report.json`` and can rename the offenders with ``-a``.

check_exports.py.summary: Compare the public definitions of a package with its ``__init__.py`` exports.
details: Scans the Python files of the given paths for the top-level functions, classes and constants, reads the ``__all__`` of the package initialisers, reports the definitions that are not exported and can add them with ``-a`` (``--dry-run`` previews).

clean-cpp.py.summary: Remove the non-essential comments and blank lines from C/C++ sources.
details: Strips the comments (keeping the ones that look essential) and collapses the blank lines of the ``.c``/``.h``/``.cc``/``.cpp``/``.hpp`` files with tree-sitter, in parallel over the given tree.
